governor.transient_model: fused-SDPA OUTPUT [q, head_dim] per layer (POST-FIX; the [q, ctx] scores term was dropped — see the fix history below)
governor.predict_path: hyperion::governor::predict_peak (the live quantized-weights path; NOT peak_within_budget, which estimates dense bf16 and would false-negative on the g64/b4 12B)

method: Per sentinel: a chunked (2048-token) prefill of synthetic zero ids at offset 0 — the production prefill path. max_predicted = the MAX predict_peak(chunk, offset) across chunks (the governor's effective admission ceiling). measured = mx::get_peak_memory() across the full chunked prefill (reset_peak_memory before). Peak memory for dense matmuls is shape-driven, so synthetic ids are valid. The gate verb is 'recorded' (10:45-46); the 20% guard is a non-gating warning that surfaces gross miscalibration.

fix_history.before_fix_transient_model: M2-2.6b modeled the SDPA ATTENTION SCORES tensor at full size [B, n_heads, q, ctx] per layer (the max(scores, output) formula).
fix_history.root_cause: MLX's mx::fast::scaled_dot_product_attention is a FUSED kernel that does NOT materialize the [q, ctx] scores matrix; it streams the computation. The M2-2.6b governor predicted a buffer that does not exist (~98-100% of the over-prediction was the transient scores term). The fused-SDPA footprint that IS materialized is the OUTPUT [q, head_dim] per layer.
fix_history.fix: attention_transient now models the OUTPUT [q, head_dim] per layer (governor.cc + predict_peak + peak_within_budget), dropping the scores term from the max(). The 1.25 kTransientSafety factor covers the fused-kernel tile working set.
fix_history.after_fix_effect: The over-prediction dropped from 2.3x (8K) / 3.6x (32K) to 1.37x (8K) / 1.34x (32K) — a ~3x improvement. The bias is now roughly CONSTANT across context (37% → 34%, vs 129% → 259% before), confirming the ctx-scaled scores term was the culprit. The governor now admits the 8K prefill comfortably (10.8 GiB predicted, under the 12 GiB budget); 32K predicts 13.1 GiB (just over the 12 GiB ceiling) vs 9.8 GiB measured — the remaining ~34% is the kWorkspaceReserve (512 MiB) + kTransientSafety (1.25x) + the live settled_working_set, a reasonable conservative admission margin.

remaining_margin: The ~34% conservative over-prediction is intentional admission headroom (the governor's purpose is to predict a bit high; it never under-admits → no OOM risk). It is NOT a further bug — the ctx-worsening trend that signaled a real bug is gone (flat across context). A future tightening (lower kTransientSafety toward 1.0 now that the output term is exact, not a worst-case scores bound) is possible if admitting 32K under the 12 GiB budget becomes a product requirement; today the 8K sentinel — the M2 G4 headline context — admits cleanly.

This artifact RECORDS the report (the gate verb) AND documents the fix the calibration motivated. The 'zero uncontrolled OOM across suite' clause (10:46) is NOT closed by this report — it requires the serving suite; the conservative bias means OOM risk is low.
